transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2025-12-06
- Start: 15:00 UTC
- Duration: 58m
- Attendees: Elena (Redwood AE), Ravi (Redwood SE), Maya (Cobalt - ML), Jonah (Cobalt - Platform), Sara (Cobalt - CTO)

Summary:
Hands-on pairing session to get Cobalt devs bootstrapped on the Redwood SDKs (Python + TypeScript), validate auth patterns for their multi-environment CI, and outline a short pilot for private VPC deployment. Quick run-through of Console, basic Optimize suggestions, and sample integration (prefix caching / batch settings).

Topics covered:
1) Quickstart repo and SDK install (pip/npm patterns)
2) API key vs. SSO/OIDC and CI secret rotation
3) Environment variables, .env + dotenv vs secrets manager patterns
4) Local dev to sandbox to prod flow; Dedicated vs Hosted tradeoffs
5) Redwood Console demo (model routing, token cost view)
6) Optimize hints (batching, KV cache, quantization suggestions)
7) Next steps and pilot scoping

Transcript body:
[00:00] Elena (Redwood): hey everyone, thanks for joining. we planned a hands-on sprint to get your team running the SDKs, auth, and a quick console tour. ravi will pair on the code bits.
[00:18] Maya (Cobalt): thanks, excited. our main blocker right now is how to wire secrets for multi-region CI and if we should start hosted or go straight to dedicated.
[00:35] Ravi (Redwood): yeah that's common — quick note, hosted is fastest for onboarding, Dedicated gives predictable throughput. for early pilot we usually recommend hosted sandbox then switch to dedicated once you lock in SLAs.
[00:52] Jonah (Cobalt): can you show the env setup? we use GitHub Actions and Hashi Vault for secrets. want to know best practice for key rotation and not leaking tokens.
[01:10] Elena (Redwood): absolutely. we'll show the pipeline pattern we use: short-lived sandbox key + repo-scoped secrets, then Vault integration in prod. also we'll share a sample GH actions job.
[01:28] Ravi (Redwood): ok jumping into the quickstart — npm install @redwood/inference and pip install redwood-inference, that's the basic. small caveat: package names differ a bit between our internal examples and the dist bundle — sometimes transcribed as "red wood" so watch the package name in the README.
[01:50] Maya (Cobalt): got it. i noticed docs mention OIDC and SAML — we use Okta, so S-S-O via SAML is our preference. how does that map to API keys?
[02:10] Elena (Redwood): you can do SAML/SSO for Console and user access. for service-to-service we recommend short-lived tokens minted by your IdP to Redwood via OIDC exchange, or use our KMS integration if you self-host. we'll send the security pack — it has the SAML/OIDC flows we're compatible with.
[02:33] Sara (Cobalt): any compliance stuff we should be aware of? audit logs, retention?
[02:40] Ravi (Redwood): yes we capture audit logs at the request level in Console; Dedicated and Private give extra retention and an option to ship logs to your SIEM. SOC 2 is supported — i'll include the compliance PDF.
[02:58] Jonah (Cobalt): cool. can we see the sample code for auth in GH actions?
[03:05] Ravi (Redwood): sure, here's the snippet i just pasted in the quickstart gist: export REDWOOD_API_KEY=\"<short-lived-key>\" then in node: const client = new RedwoodClient({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY, region: 'us-west-2' }); note: in local dev we suggest .env with dotenv, but in CI use GH secrets or Vault; don't commit .env.
[03:35] Elena (Redwood): and for TypeScript we show both fetch wrappers and our official SDK client. sample ts code is in /examples/ts/quickstart.
[03:50] Maya (Cobalt): are there rate limits on sandbox keys? we have bursty traffic during batch jobs.
[03:58] Elena (Redwood): sandbox has soft limits; Dedicated gives reserved GPU pools and predictable throughput. you can also configure burst capacity. we'll put numbers into the follow-up doc.
[04:12] Jonah (Cobalt): re: caching — you mentioned KV cache earlier, does that mean we need a separate cache service?
[04:20] Ravi (Redwood): no, Redwood runtime does prefix/K V cache for inference, it's automatic for compatible models. sometimes the notes say K V cash or K V cache — transcription aside — but the important bit is: caching reduces token cost for repeated prefixes. can configure TTLs via the route.
[04:45] Maya (Cobalt): ok nice. show us the console where we can pin model versions and see token cost.
[04:55] Elena (Redwood): sharing my screen — here's Console, per-route view, cost by token, latency percentiles. model routing is here: you can set primary model, fallback, and a canary rollout percent. note the Optimize suggestions tab — it shows batch size/quantization recs based on your workload profile. (screen share brief pause)
[05:25] Ravi (Redwood): just flagging one gotcha we see in early pilots — prompt size plus concurrency influences kernel selection; our runtime picks different kernels and that affects latency. Optimize will suggest sequence length caps and batching thresholds.
[05:45] Jonah (Cobalt): how do we measure e2e latency — app to model?
[05:50] Ravi (Redwood): Console traces request time breakdown: client -> network -> runtime -> model. we also emit spans you can hook into your tracer.
[06:05] Maya (Cobalt): for the SDK quickstart, can we walk through a small python example?
[06:10] Ravi (Redwood): yep. python sample: from redwood_inference import Client; c = Client(api_key=os.environ.get('REDWOOD_API_KEY')); resp = c.generate(model='rw-medium', input='summarize...') note: model handles differ — our catalog has "rw-medium" in examples; real model id may be redwood-... in Console. sometimes folks transcribe it as "rw med"
[06:35] Elena (Redwood): we also covered embedding generation in the repo — python and ts both have a fast path for embeddings with batching helpers.
[06:45] Jonah (Cobalt): embedding throughput is key for our search feature — any suggestions to optimize cost?
[06:50] Ravi (Redwood): batch embeddings on the client side to maximize tokens/req, and use quantized models for lower precision if semantic quality tolerates it. Optimize will recommend quantization levels based on evals you run.
[07:10] Maya (Cobalt): speaking of evals, can we attach our prompt set to the Optimize monitor?
[07:15] Elena (Redwood): yes, you can upload prompt/eval sets in Console; Optimize will run regression checks and alert on quality drops. we'll share a short guide in the follow-up.
[07:30] Sara (Cobalt): timeline question — if we want Dedicated by end of January, is that realistic?
[07:36] Elena (Redwood): yes, realistic if you complete pilot in December. Dedicated requires capacity planning and a short onboarding for network/VPC. we can start sandbox hosted now, then Dedicated onboarding in Jan.
[07:50] Jonah (Cobalt): network — we need VPC peering and a private deployment option for some PII workloads. what's the private offering?
[07:58] Ravi (Redwood): Private gives VPC or on-prem. for VPC we provide the control plane hooks and optional on-prem package. KMS/HSM integrations supported. some docs call it Private or Private Deploy. we'll send the network checklist.
[08:20] Maya (Cobalt): any gotchas with Okta SAML and short-lived keys?
[08:25] Elena (Redwood): if you leverage OIDC token exchange it's smoother. SAML can be used for console SSO; for service tokens we recommend OIDC or vault-minted keys. we'll include sample exchange flow in the security doc.
[08:40] Ravi (Redwood): quick demo of switching environments — i have a sandbox key, switching region in the client is just region param. in prod you'd point to your dedicated endpoint or private endpoint.
[09:00] Elena (Redwood): ok let's do a short pairing task — maya, can you run the TS quickstart and paste any errors in chat so ravi can triage?
[09:12] Maya (Cobalt): starting now... npm i @redwood/inference ... installing... seeing a TypeError referencing fetch in Node 14 environment.
[09:25] Ravi (Redwood): ah that's expected — our TS client expects Node >=16 and a global fetch polyfill for 16/18. add node-fetch or upgrade node in CI. i'll add that note to the quickstart.
[09:45] Maya (Cobalt): ok after polyfill i get auth error 401: invalid key. i copied the sandbox key from the convo but maybe it expired.
[09:55] Elena (Redwood): sandbox keys are short-lived; i'm sending a fresh key to the shared secure channel now. use the new key and try again.
[10:05] Maya (Cobalt): re-run — success. generating sample embedding now, returns 512-d vector. perfect.
[10:20] Sara (Cobalt): great progress. any notes on token cost forecasting?
[10:25] Ravi (Redwood): Console's cost tab projects token spend by route, you can attach budgets. Optimize will show cost per 1k tokens estimates for model variants.
[10:40] Elena (Redwood): closing thoughts — pilot scope: run hosted sandbox integration for two weeks with 3 endpoints (chat, embeddings, reranker), measure latency and cost, then plan Dedicated onboarding if numbers align.
[10:58] Jonah (Cobalt): agreed. we'll confirm internal stakeholders and timeline.
[11:05] Elena (Redwood): ok next steps recap: i'll share quickstart repo, sandbox key, security pack; ravi will send perf checklist and sample GH action; maya to share prompt set and target SLOs.
[11:25] Maya (Cobalt): thanks everyone. appreciate the pairing.
[11:30] Elena (Redwood): thanks all — we'll follow up in email with links.
